about: Eval briefs for concept-driven motion (does the motion express what the mark depicts?). Move into evals/ once the eval harness is merged. setup = editor tool calls that build the artwork before the brief is sent; parts are named neutrally (Path 1..n) on purpose, so the agent has to look at them.

judge.question: Does the motion express what the mark depicts and fit the brand, instead of generic pop/fade/scale-ins?
rubric: concept: the hero action is the depicted object's own action (see expect.concept); generic pop/fade/scale on every part scores 1
pivots: parts move around physically plausible pivots (hinge, base, stem, tail tip)
brand fit: easing/timing match the brand traits named in the brief
process: the agent looked at the artwork (inspect_artwork / contact_sheet / screenshot) before animating and named the parts
concepts offered: 2-3 one-line concepts (or propose_storyboard concepts) with a recommendation
integrity: the final frame equals the original lockup (positions, rotations, scales, colors)

briefs.brief: Animate our logo for the app intro (about 3 s). Brand: Haven, home rentals; warm and welcoming.

expect.concept: the door (Path 2) swings open on a hinge edge (anchor at its left or right edge, scale x / skew), maybe light or the wordmark coming out of it

briefs.brief: Make a 3 second logo animation for Sprout, an organic baby-food brand. Calm and natural.

expect.concept: the stem draws/grows up from its base, leaves unfurl from the stem (pivot at the leaf base), gentle sway; wordmark follows calmly

briefs.brief: Animate the Huddle logo (a team chat app) for a 3 s splash screen. Friendly and lively.

expect.concept: the bubble pops from its tail tip (pivot at the tail), the three dots bounce like typing, then resolve into the wordmark

briefs.brief: Logo sting for Liftoff, a startup accelerator. 3 seconds, energetic and confident.

expect.concept: anticipation (squash/dip), flame flickers (Path 3), the rocket launches upward with acceleration and lands/settles into the lockup or exits and returns; split_shape the two fins (Path 2 is one compound path)
